newsitem.title: USA: ING eyes large U.S. life insurance buy. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ING eyes large U.S. life insurance buy. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Dutch financial services firm Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV is willing to pay "more than a couple of billion dollars" to make a life insurance acquisition in the United States, chairman Aad Jacobs said.

Jacobs, speaking to reporters following the company's listing on the New York Stock Exchange, said he would be most interested in acquiring a life insurance company with a strong presence in the variable annuity or term (corrects from "variable") insurance market.
Jacobs told analysts in Amsterdam several weeks ago that ING was talking to several U.S. life insurers, but declined to identify them.
Jacobs on Friday said the New York listing will allow the company to use its shares, in addition to cash, as currency for an acquisition.
"If we are going to make an acquisition in the future, then we can pay with our own shares," Jacobs said.
But, he said the company did not have any immediate plans to issue new shares to finance a deal.
"It depends on the size of the company we are interested in," he said. "We are quite a rich company so we can pay a lot out of our own pockets without the assistance of shareholders," he said.
"If it is a bigger issue, then probably we have to pay partly in shares. But we always will look very carefully that it will have no drain on our earnings per share," he said.
But, he said, he believes it is important to increase ING's presence in the U.S. insurance market.

"This is by far the most important insurance market in the world, not only in size, but also technology, also in innovation; products that are invented here come later to the European market," he said.
"So you have to be an important player in the American market," he said.
Jacobs said he did not have any particular geographic preference.
But he said the company was interested in a life company, with variable annuity and term insurance products.
Although ING has said it was in talks with several U.S. life insurers, it was not immediately clear how close a deal might be.
Sources in the United States were not aware of any life insurance properties that were currently being marketed.
Analysts and bankers have speculated that Aetna Inc and CIGNA Corp might be willing to sell their life insurance businesses.
Aetna declined immediate comment. CIGNA was not immediately available for comment.
Torchmark Corp also could be a possible takeover target, some analysts said. Torchmark was not immediately available for comment.
